reading.body:
Crane DC - Portland, located in Forest Grove, Oregon, publishes 36,000 square feet of technical space but no IT load figure in megawatts. Without a published power number, no translation to rack count or accelerator capacity is possible, and this campus does not appear among the six Oregon facilities that have published a megawatt figure, which together total 182 MW. The absence of a power specification is common across the state: 133 facilities are mapped in Oregon, and only six have published any capacity number at all.

The seven certifications on record qualify the campus to host specific workload categories. PCI DSS qualifies it for payment card data. FISMA and NIST 800-53 together qualify it for federal information systems. HITRUST qualifies it for healthcare information. ISO 27001 and SSAE 18 qualify it for enterprise tenants requiring audited information security management and controls reporting. LEED indicates the building met a green construction or operations standard at the time of certification.

For an AI decision, the missing power number is the central fact. Compute density for training workloads is the binding constraint, and 36,000 square feet of technical space could support very different capacities depending on power delivery, cooling infrastructure, and floor loading, none of which are published. The compliance portfolio suggests the operator targets regulated enterprise and government workloads rather than hyperscale AI training, but that inference rests on the certification mix alone, not on any published tenant or use-case claim.
